correctness.rationale: Weyl-covariant Fourier diagonalization determines every lifted singular value as sqrt(n) times a normalized ambiguity magnitude. For odd composite n all residue products ab are attained by a,b nonzero: units cover j!=0 and zero divisors cover j=0. The uniform phase grid bounds the mixed margin by sin(pi/(2n)); AM-GM in the radius and cos(phi)>=-1 yield the global sharp upper bound. At unique parameter z=-sqrt(n), the mixed minimum attains it, and both unmixed coefficients n-2sqrt(n) exceed that mixed minimum for n>=9. Direct full 81x81 lifting SVD n=9 and 978 checker assertions corroborate. The proof covers every odd composite n and every complex z; finite checks alone are not treated as proof.

value.rationale: A natural arithmetic classification of the best-conditioned one-defect Gabor measurement design requires a third regime: odd composite, alongside distinct known prime and even-composite regimes. The result supplies exact all-order optimal reconstruction constants, a unique real hardware parameter, and a phase-grid mechanism via zero divisors, rather than merely another rank criterion or arbitrary finite calculation. This precise stability optimum is relevant to noise amplification for a simple physically implementable structured window family; optimality is restricted to this family.
